title: Positive-control verification of Algorithm 1 and the finite-sample theorem under a restricted role-blind representation class

representation_class.rule: one retained block is the channel
representation_class.formula: Phi_S = {(x1, x2, w_j) : j not in S}
representation_class.note: closed under block permutation; contains no block role

screen.objective: max{R_0 - R_1, 0} for nested probit-linear Brier critics on I_D
screen.nested_by: the augmented fit starts from the base fit with zero weight on W_S

budget.note: every split is drawn, so R equals N

evaluation.nuisance: exact, closed form under the true law

structure.rationale: the manuscript theorem is conditional on the learning sample, so the screen and the retained set are fixed once per learning state

seeds.note: no seed in these blocks has been generated by any earlier run

reporting_rules: Every quantity of the theorem is recomputed on the realised retained set of each state: N, Delta, L, g_min, rho.
A tied-largest return or a candidate set counts as a failure.
A state that retains a split outside the population candidate set, or selects a beta other than the population minimiser, is recorded as theorem-condition FAIL and reported.
The observed success rate is compared with the manuscript bound 1 - delta - P(R=0) - L E[exp(-R Delta^2 / 2)] evaluated at the realised N, Delta and L.
claim_boundary: Positive-control verification of Algorithm 1 and the finite-sample theorem under a restricted role-blind representation class with exact nuisance. It is not a claim about representation learning in general; SCM-6 and SCM-7 carry that role.
